sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.
Heard Sri. Hiremathad Maheshiah Rudrayya, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.
Waheeda M. M., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent/State.

2. The petitioner/accused No.1, husband of the deceased is seeking regular bail in Crime No.348/2023 wherein the respondent/police registered a case against the petitioner for the offences under sections 302 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').

The charge sheet is filed for the offences punishable under Sections 302, 498-A, 306 r/w 34 of IPC pending on the file of IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, Shivamogga (Sitting at Bhadravathi) in S.C No.5021/2024.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Shivamogga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Brief facts of the case are as under:
3. It is the case of the prosecution that Sri.Chandrappa S/o Guddappa lodged a complaint stating that he performed the marriage of his daughter with accused No.1, ten years ago.
The couple had male child aged about 7 years NC: 2024:KHC:26461 and daughter aged about 5 years.

It is further stated in the complaint that the petitioner and his family members were harassing the deceased both mentally and physically since the date of marriage and she was being tortured in one or the other pretext.
4. On 27.11.2023, around 11.00 a.m., the complainant had received a message stating that his daughter committed suicide in the matrimonial home by hanging.
He went to the spot and after seeing dead body of his daughter, he lodged a complaint against the petitioner herein and others.
The jurisdictional police, initially, registered a case in Crime No.348/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 302 r/w 34 of IPC.
After investigation, they arrived at a conclusion that the deceased had committed suicide by hanging.
Therefore, the jurisdictional police inserted the provision under Sections 498-A, 306 r/w 34 of IPC by deleting the provision under Section 302 of IPC.
Thereafter, charge sheet came to be filed.
5. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in this NC: 2024:KHC:26461 case and he is innocent of the alleged offences.
In fact, the cause of death was not known to the petitioner herein.

The complainant being the father of the deceased and having been influenced by others, he lodged a complaint against the petitioner and his family members in respect of the offence under Section 302 of IPC, however, during investigation,

sentences.text:
the jurisdictional police deleted the provision under Section 302 of IPC and incorporated Sections 498-A and 306 r/w 34 of IPC.
6.
It is further submitted that on reading of the complaint, even the provision under Section 306 of IPC would not attract against the petitioner.
In fact, there is no nexus between the death and alleged harassment and cruelty meted out to her.
7. The petitioner is the permanent resident of Tadasa Village, Holehonnur Hobli, Bhadravathi Taluk and he is aged about 33 years.
He has to take care of his children and also aged parents and he will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted that the petitioner being the husband of the victim, he was torturing her in one or the other pretext.
As the victim could not tolerate such cruelty, she committed suicide by leaving two children.
Prima facie, the offence to commit suicide has been established by filing the charge sheet.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any relief as prayed for.
Making such submissions, the learned High Court Government Pleader prays to dismiss the petition.

9. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet and also other relevant documents, it appears on the record that the father of the deceased being the complainant, had lodged a complaint stating that the petitioner and others have killed his daughter.
Later, during investigation, it appeared that the deceased committed suicide.
Though the complainant made several allegations against the petitioner and family members, on careful reading of the entire documents, there is no material placed to justify the charge sheet.

Without adverting to the merits of the case, having considered the NC: 2024:KHC:26461 averments of the charge sheet, prima facie, I am of the opinion that the petitioner made out a case to grant him bail.

10. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No. 348/2023 of respondent Police Station in S.C No.5021/2024 pending on the file of IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, Shivamogga (Sitting at Bhadravathi) on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court regularly without fail.
